restaurant: 鸡煲之家 Chicken Claypot House (Sunway Pyramid)
review_text:
Short review:
Sesame Chicken Claypot ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Suancai Fish ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Long review:
In my 4th visit, I decided not to go for those chicken hotpot options and settled for a sesame chicken claypot and suancai fish. Yes, even Chicken Claypot House cannot deny the popularity of this dish now in Malaysia and has introduced it into their menu as a seasonal offer.
Sesame Chicken Claypot ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
I thoroughly enjoyed this dish. The sauce was really savory with just enough of that sesame taste. In addition to that, the finely chopped and pre-fried ginger gave this dish that extra fragrant taste. So it was not good for my dieting plan as I ended up having two and a half bowl of rice just because of it. The chicken was also pre-marinated I believe. It was flavorful although the kitchen staff gave me mostly chicken breast.

One criticism I have for this restaurant is its rice. It's very lumpy and has limited the joy of having this sauce on the rice. 1 star for the rice.

Suancai Fish ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
For this dish, it came in a humongous bowl. There's not a lot of fish slices but the quality of the fish is there. No earthy taste unlike Tai Er. For me, that is my number one criteria when it comes to eating fish. To be fair to Tai Er, the first and the last time I was there was about one and half years ago. I hope things have changed now for them. Coming back to Chicken Claypot House's version, the peppercorn soup gives you quite the heat after consuming it for a while. But it was good and I like the fact that the sourish taste did not go overboard as to render it acidic in taste. Another important thing to note is that it did not come with a THICK layer of oil unlike the others that I have tried before. So I did not have to spend time filtering away the oil. So it does hold up well to other restaurants that specialize in this dish.

For this dish, it came in a humongous bowl. There's not a lot of fish slices but the quality of the fish is there. No earthy taste unlike Tai Er. For me, that is my number one criteria when it comes to eating fish. To be fair to Tai Er, the first and the last time I was there was about one and half years ago. I hope things have changed now for them. Coming back to Chicken Claypot House's version, the peppercorn soup gives you quite the heat after consuming it for a while. But it was good and I like the fact that the sourish taste did not go overboard as to render it acidic in taste. Another important thing to note is that it did not come with a THICK layer of oil unlike the others that I have tried before. So I did not have to spend time filtering away the oil. So it does hold up well to other restaurants that specialize in this dish.

restaurant: Luo Ma Claypot
review_text:
SS15 ….. just take a stroll here and you will be spoilt for choice for food, desert and what-have-yous. From the oriental to western to eastern. Take your pick.
Tucked amongst these is Luoma Claypot. This is a chain of restaurants serving Chengdu fare.
Along with a service fee of RM2 per head, you get free flow of drinks and pickled vegetables. Also a great deal if you are on a cheat day and want to load up on your carbohydrates! Yes ….. the rice comes free flow as well!
Now on to the food. Dishes are served in claypots and this retains the heat and flavour of the food.
For first timers, the eggplant with minced claypot will certainly be a treat. When it arrives, give it a quick stir to coat everything in that thick gravy. The rich, deep umami flavour pairs perfectly with steamed rice.
Next up is the spicy stir-fried pork with chilli peppers. You can choose less spicy should you wish. This is basically thin slices of pork seared in high heat with a generous supply of chillies and peppers. The pork is nice and savoury while the chilli and peppers give it just a right amount of zing. This is one dish that makes you want to eat more rice than usual. Did I mention about loading up on carbohydrates? Hahaha……
The cherry braised pork is also another crowd favourite. This dish is not spicy – but just watch out for the thick layer of fat. But what the heck – if it is your cheat day, it does not matter anyway.
The restaurant’s setting is very minimalist. No fanciful decorations and stuff like that.
The staff comprise of mostly young adults and are very friendly and helpful.

review_text:
整体体验不错。店内走复古中式风格，墙上贴满中文报纸，搭配木质桌椅，氛围很有感觉，也比较干净舒适。

RM2的餐位费包含白饭、泡菜、酸梅汤和中国茶，可以无限续，这点蛮加分的，性价比不错。

整体来说，如果喜欢重口味、川菜风味，这家值得一试。
review_text_english: Overall a good experience. The retro Chinese interior has newspaper-covered walls and wooden tables and chairs; clean and comfortable. Claypot dishes are cooked fresh and arrive bubbling hot. Flavours are bold but not overly salty, aromatic, and spice levels are adjustable. We ordered garlic vermicelli prawns, twice-cooked pork and braised beef brisket; all were flavourful and excellent with rice. The RM2 table charge includes unlimited rice, pickles, sour plum drink and Chinese tea, making it good value. Worth trying for lovers of bold Sichuan flavours.

restaurant: Luo Ma Claypot
review_text:
Subang Jaya’s unofficial Chengdu teleportation device. Walk in and forget windows exist; the walls are covered in kitschy Chinese newspaper prints like someone said, “Let’s fake Chengdu in Malaysia.” Students dominate the crowd, hunched over steaming claypots like exam notes, and honestly, it feels like half the town’s caffeine-fueled youth decided to make spicy food their religion.

Claypots arrive sizzling, aromatic, borderline violent in presentation: Cherry Braised Pork, Eggplant with Minced Pork, Tomato Meatball Soup, Mapo Tofu. Free-flow rice and pickled cabbage are not optional, they are survival gear. Prices RM 20-40, portions so generous your stomach files a complaint before the food does.

Luo Ma started in Chengdu decades ago and now has hundreds of branches worldwide, mostly in China, making this Malaysian outpost a tiny embassy of chaos and spice. Come for the food, stay to wonder why your tongue is plotting revenge, and leave smelling like you survived a Sichuan fire drill.

review_text:
Had a really great experience here!

The food was surprisingly flavorful and well-balanced especially the soup, which was rich, comforting, and full of ingredients.

You can really taste the freshness.

The claypot dish was another highlight nicely cooked, aromatic, and packed with flavor. Portions were generous and served hot, which made everything even better.

The environment is clean, bright, and comfortable, perfect for a casual meal. Service was friendly and efficient too.

Definitely a place I would come back again 👍
Highly recommended if you’re looking for tasty, satisfying comfort food!
